thread:
cheng: Quick sync — we're planning a CP split where smaller tenants get their own lightweight controlplane in-customer-VPC. Main concerns: DNS delegation timing, cert rotation batching (to avoid flooding customer KMS/HSM requests), and how a minimal sidecar should behave for fallback. Thoughts? :thinking:

alex: high level +1. two quick Qs: do we expect tenant DNS to be authoritative (ns delegation) or just conditional forwarders? that changes cert issuance pattern a lot.

maria: if we do ns delegation, cert rotation needs to avoid reissuing during zone transfers. prefer a single rotation controller that batches per-tenant and per-region.

sanjay: agree on batching. naive idea: gate cert ops behind a token bucket per-tenant and a per-region queue. batch window 60s by default. reduces KMS ops and peak latency.

cheng: alex — leaning toward NS delegation for true isolation (customer owns zone) but we'd still write glue records. downside is rollout complexity. maria/sanjay — can you sketch how rotation controller APIs look?

maria: something like:```\nPOST /v1/tenants/:id/cert-rotate\n{\n  \"type\": \"leaf\",\n  \"batch_key\": \"region-us-west-2\",\n  \"requested_at\": \"2026-03-23T12:00:00Z\"\n}\n```controller enqueues and picks up batches every 60s, groups by batch_key, and performs single KMS unwrap call per batch where possible. Response is async op id.

cheng: nice. what about rollover semantics? ideally we create new certs, add to endpoint, allow 10m overlap, then revoke old. can we do with customers that have strict ACLs?

sanjay: for strict ACLs we need a handshake: create cert, surface thumbprint to customer, they whitelist before we activate. might be manual for some early-enterprise tenants. automation can fall back to \"whitelist-required\" flag in tenant config.

kirby: small note re DNS: if we flip NS delegation, we must handle transient DNS failures — fallback to synthetic DNS entries served by Redwood for 5m while delegation updates propagate. Otherwise a quick rollback is painful.

alex: also consider mTLS termination placement. two options: (A) terminate mTLS at tenant-side sidecar (we prefer sidecarless, but may be required), or (B) do termination in customer CP instance and keep short-lived client certs for dataplane. Option B gives better isolation but needs cert distribution in customer VPC.

cheng: prefer keep-aside minimal proxy that only does cert handshake and health checks, no heavy routing. Sidecarless is long-term goal but can't block rollout. Any operational runbooks to add?

maria: runbook sketch: 1) create tenant CP in staging VPC; 2) push DNS glue + delegation; 3) deploy cert controller with batch window 60s; 4) enable synthetic DNS fallback for 5m; 5) enable observability (dns propagation metric, cert-batch-latency).

kirby: add a throttling rule for KMS/HSM: if KMS error rate spikes > 5% for 2m, pause rotations and mark tenant \"degraded-cert-ops\" with alert to secops.

cheng: good. what about rollback for half-caught rollouts when delegation partially applied?

sanjay: we should make all CP config changes idempotent and use a blue/green activation marker. steps: provision new cp, register it but keep weight=0, wait for DNS to serve new NS, then flip weight->100. if anything fails flip back weight->0.

alex: short snippet for weight flip using our control plane tool:
```\n# set weight 0\nredwoodctl cp set-weight --tenant $TID --cp $CP_ID --weight 0\n# wait for propagation\nsleep 30\n# set weight 100\nredwoodctl cp set-weight --tenant $TID --cp $CP_ID --weight 100\n```

maria: add health-check gating: only flip if probe success > 95% across 3 consecutive polls.

cheng: ok action items: - maria/sanjay draft cert-controller CRD + batch semantics (include token bucket/queue) - alex to draft DNS delegation playbook + glue record verification steps - kirby to add KMS throttling/alert thresholds to SecOps runbook - I'll prototype synthetic DNS fallback in staging.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: \"staging/synthetic-dns-fallback\" started by cheng at 2026-03-23T12:05:10Z :rocket:

alex: one more: telemetry. we need per-tenant metrics: cert_ops_rate, cert_ops_errors, dns_delegate_latency, delegation_rollback_count. anything else?

maria: include \"batch_size\" and \"avg_batch_duration\" so we can tune window.

cheng: thanks all. Will schedule RFC follow-up next Tue 10am to review CRD and playbooks. :thumbsup:
